## Summary

Important finding up front: the current runtime implementation and the acceptance-test spec disagree. The test file describes "identity-key-v2" (a 64-char SHA-256 hex over `normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName)`), but the actual `Owner.getIdentityKey()` returns a plaintext `telephone|email|householdId` string that is neither SHA-256-hashed nor soundex-based. There is no Soundex utility anywhere in the codebase. Details below.

---

### 1. Where identityKey is computed

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` lines 309-322:

```java
@Transient
public String getIdentityKey() {
    return this.telephone + "|"
        + (this.email == null ? "" : this.email) + "|"
        + (this.householdId == null ? "" : this.householdId);
}
```

This is the ONLY place identityKey is produced. It is plaintext, NOT SHA-256, and uses `householdId` (which itself derives from lastName+postcode), not `soundex(lastName)`. `email` is stored lower-cased via `setEmail` (lines 171-173): `email.toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT)`. The identityKey is exposed on the DTO by `OwnerMapper` (line 39): `@Mapping(target = "identityKey", expression = "java(owner.getIdentityKey())")` in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java`.

Note the mismatch: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` lines 9-19 asserts `key.matches("[0-9a-f]{64}")` (a 64-hex SHA-256) and the header comment states the key is `SHA-256 hex over (normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName))`. The current plaintext implementation will not satisfy that regex, and no soundex is applied.

### 2. Where duplicate detection returns 409

Controller `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`, in `addOwner`, lines 138-142:

```java
if (this.clinicService.existsOwnerWithIdentityKey(owner)) {
    return new ResponseEntity<>(HttpStatus.CONFLICT);
}
```

The backing check is `ClinicServiceImpl.existsOwnerWithIdentityKey` in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java` lines 261-271:

```java
public boolean existsOwnerWithIdentityKey(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
    String identityKey = owner.getIdentityKey();
    return ownerRepository.findByTelephone(owner.getTelephone()).stream()
        .filter(existing -> !existing.isDeleted())
        .anyMatch(existing -> identityKey.equals(existing.getIdentityKey()));
}
```

The only other 409/CONFLICT in the codebase is the city-capacity check at line 131-133 of the same controller (`isCityAtCapacity`), not a duplicate check.

### 3. Where householdId is computed / household-duplicate block

householdId generation: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/HouseholdIdGenerator.java` lines 43-46:

```java
public String generate(String lastName, String postcode) {
    String key = canonical(lastName) + "|" + (postcode == null ? "" : postcode);
    return Sha256.hex(key).substring(0, 12);
}
```

`canonical` (lines 53-55) trims, collapses whitespace, lower-cases the last name. Assignment happens in `ClinicServiceImpl.assignHousehold` lines 358-367 (returns null when no postcode), called from the controller at line 136.

There is no separate "household-duplicate 409" block. Household membership only feeds `householdSize`/`membershipLevel`/`identityKey`. The household members are gathered in `ClinicServiceImpl.findHouseholdMembers` lines 402-410 (same lastName ignoring case + same postcode, excluding deleted), used by `countHouseholdMembers` (376-378) and `resolveCappedMembershipLevel` (385-394). The household participates in duplicate rejection only indirectly, because `householdId` is one of the three components of `getIdentityKey()` checked in item 2.

### 4. Soft-match logic (postcode + lastName)

`ClinicServiceImpl.findPossibleDuplicateOwnerId` lines 279-292:

```java
public Integer findPossibleDuplicateOwnerId(Owner owner) throws DataAccessException {
    if (owner.getPostcode() == null) {
        return null;
    }
    return ownerRepository.findByLastNameIgnoreCase(owner.getLastName()).stream()
        .filter(existing -> !existing.isDeleted())
        .filter(existing -> owner.getPostcode().equals(existing.getPostcode()))
        .filter(existing -> !Objects.equals(owner.getTelephone(), existing.getTelephone()))
        .map(Owner::getId)
        .min(Integer::compareTo)
        .orElse(null);
}
```

Note: the soft-match uses `findByLastNameIgnoreCase` (exact last-name equality ignoring case) plus postcode plus differing telephone. It does NOT use soundex, despite the test comment referring to soundex. Wired in the controller at lines 152-156, guarded by `declaredHouseholdMember` (from `ownerFieldsDto.getSharesHousehold()`), setting `possibleDuplicate` / `possibleDuplicateOf` on the owner.

### 5. Where "deleted" owners are filtered

Soft-delete flag lives on `Owner` (field `deleted`, lines 98-99; `isDeleted`/`setDeleted` 296-307). Set true in `ClinicServiceImpl.deleteOwner` lines 153-160 (record retained, `owner.setDeleted(true)` then saved). Deleted owners are filtered out via `!existing.isDeleted()` in three places in `ClinicServiceImpl.java`:
- `existsOwnerWithIdentityKey` line 269 (duplicate/409 check)
- `findPossibleDuplicateOwnerId` line 286 (soft-match)
- `findHouseholdMembers` line 407 (household size / membership)

The delete endpoint is `OwnerRestControllerV1.deleteOwner` lines 196-206.

### 6. Email-domain blocklist logic

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/DisposableEmailRule.java` lines 14-42. Blocked domains are a fixed set (lines 17-20): `mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`. `isDisposable` takes the substring after the last `@`, lower-cases it (Locale.ROOT), and checks set membership; null email or no `@` returns false.

Wiring: the Bean Validation constraint annotation `NotDisposableEmail` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/NotDisposableEmail.java`) and its validator `DisposableEmailValidator` (`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/validation/DisposableEmailValidator.java`, delegates to `DisposableEmailRule.isDisposable`).

### 7. Relevant test files

- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` — `coreIdentityKeyIsSha256Hex` (asserts 64-hex identityKey) and `coreRejectsDuplicateIdentity` (asserts 409 on identical telephone/email/lastName). Header comment (lines 9-11) states the intended identity-key-v2 = `SHA-256 hex over (normalizedTelephone | lowerEmail | soundex(lastName))`.
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` — the black-box harness: `createOwner`/`createOwnerOk`, `fetchOwner`, `deleteOwner` (soft-delete helper, lines 193-197), `structuredOwner()`/`ownerNode()` payload builders, `uniqueEmail`, and reference `sha256hex`/`shaHex`/`luhn` implementations (lines 281-321).
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AuditLogCapture.java` — matched the keyword grep (audit-related; adjacent to owner-creation auditing via `OwnerAuditor`).
